refnamediv.refpurpose: Report the approximate geographic location of the system as system report metrics

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: systemd-report-geoip@.service is a metrics source for systemd-report1. It reports the approximate geographic location of the system, as determined by a public IP geolocation web service from the public IP address the system connects to it with. It implements the io.systemd.Metrics Varlink interface on a socket linked into the /run/systemd/report/ directory.

The geolocation data is acquired via HTTP from the endpoint configured in report-geoip.conf5. The acquired data is cached, and only refreshed once the cache is older than the configured RefreshSec= interval. If the endpoint cannot be reached, the cached data is reported even if it is older than that. If no data is available at all, no metrics are reported. The network request is subject to a short timeout, so that a slow or unreachable endpoint does not delay report generation unduly.

refsect1.title: Metrics
refsect1.para: The following metrics are reported, all in the io.systemd.GeoIP. namespace. Fields the geolocation service does not provide (or provides empty) are not reported.

listitem.para: The public IP address of the system, as seen by the geolocation service. The address is validated and reported in normalized form.
The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code and the name of the country the system is located in.
The code and name of the region (state, province, …) the system is located in.
The city and postal code of the area the system is located in.
The IANA time zone name of the area the system is located in.
The geographic coordinates of the system's location, in decimal degrees.

The time at which the reported data was acquired from the geolocation service, in microseconds since the UNIX epoch (CLOCK_REALTIME). When the data is served from the cache this is the time the cache was last refreshed, not the time of the report.

refsect1.title: Privacy
refsect1.para: Note that refreshing the geolocation data means contacting a third party web service, which thereby learns the public IP address of the system. The reported metrics identify the system's public IP address and approximate location, and hence are sensitive. Only enable this service if this is acceptable for the systems the reports are collected from.
